Asia-Pacific demand was also high this week for Brazilian crude, with at least eight VLCCs provisionally hired by charterers in that spot market.

Midsize rates climb on VLCC spillover
Rising freight rates for VLCCs in the west Africa spot market, which shares a tonnage pool with the Brazilian market, encouraged charterers to explore splitting these 2mn bl cargoes onto two 1mn bl Suezmax tankers on 2 September, according to a shipbroker.
Meanwhile, Aframax shipments of WTI crude from the US Gulf coast into Europe have been trading at, and even below, parity with VLCC-sized shipments of WTI on the same route on a $/bl basis.
Aframax tankers typically trade at a premium to VLCCs in this context given the greater number of ports the smaller tanker can access and its ease in loading and unloading compared to VLCCs. The last time Aframax-sized shipments of WTI into Europe were cheaper than VLCCs on the same route was in February 2021.
The surge in VLCC demand from Asia-Pacific will likely encourage US Gulf coast buyers globally to increasingly consider the midsize segment in the near term, maintaining the upward pressure on rates for Aframaxes and Suezmaxes even after the long holiday weekend for US traders.

candidates.title: VLCC Rates Hit Record $1.27 Million a Day as Oman Transfer Capacity Maxes Out | OilPrice.com
candidates.source_name: VLCC Rates Hit Record $1.27 Million a Day as Oman Transfer Capacity Maxes Out | OilPrice.com
candidates.snippet:
By Irina Slav - Sep 25, 2026, 1:17 AM CDT
Capacity for ship-to-ship transfers of crude oil off the coast of Oman has reached its limits after Saudi Arabia diverted its flows from the port of Yanbu amid Houthi attacks, Reuters has reported , citing unnamed trading sources and analysts.
The report said Saudi Arabia has sold some 60 million barrels of crude, to be shipped from the Gulf of Oman after being transferred from smaller carriers to supertankers, for delivery this month and in October. This has tightened an already tight very large crude carrier market and led to a further increase in oil shipping costs.
The ship-to-ship transfer route involves loading crude at a Persian Gulf coast, shipping it across the Strait of Hormuz and transferring the cargo to a larger tanker in the safer Gulf of Oman. The daily rate so far in September has been averaging 3.6 million barrels, according to Kpler.
This is up from just 900,000 barrels daily in August, before the Yemeni Houthis attacked the East-West pipeline.
This amount of crude needs between 36 and 40 additional very large crude carriers, Kpler analyst Panagiotis Krontiras told the publication.
The analyst explained that exporting the same amount of oil that in August required 24 VLCCs, in September requires 40 very large crude carriers because of the ship-to-ship transfers.
To make the tanker availability situation worse, there are 20 tankers sitting in the Red Sea waiting for the port of Yanbu to resume operations.

What bringing your own power solves
Idle GPUs cost far more than the electricity to run them, so speed matters most — what folks call “time to power.” That’s why developers are planning to bring their own power on site (“behind the meter”), but almost always alongside a connection to the grid, or as a bridge to one:
* Pecos County: Pacifico describes its planned microgrid (a behind-the-meter setup) at GW Ranch as never drawing from ERCOT , yet the site’s new owner, Amazon, says it’s designed to join the grid once it can connect.
SemiAnalysis is already tracking 75 GW of equipment orders for behind-the-meter assets, but every site I’m aware of intends to connect to the grid as soon as it can, chiefly because on-site power almost always costs more. So, once the grid is available, say in year five, you switch.
Expect more batteries and other energy storage as rack-level power density grows and swings become more dramatic.
Then there’s fueling a site. Winter Storm Uri’s lesson is that gas plants can fail together . And since they tend to keep little fuel on site (NERC calls gas a “just-in-time” fuel ), spare turbines don’t always help.
Thus, behind-the-meter setups favor modularity, like the more than 500 gas engines of about 4 MW each planned for Shackelford, though hundreds of engines can be a pain to maintain.
Full reliability for an island is very, very hard, but some labs and hyperscalers have shown that, forced to choose between reliability and speed, they’ll pick speed.

The European Space Agency has selected the ICEYE-led ARISE consortium to design the architecture for the EU Earth Observation Governmental Service, a planned sovereign space-based intelligence system for European civil security and defence users.
The partners combine operational systems with institutional and national capabilities across defence, security, classified Earth Observation, dual-use operations, sovereign cloud and data infrastructure, system accreditation, intelligence analytics, and mission and upstream development.
“This contract advances a more sovereign and resilient European capability, fully aligned with Indra’s strategy to develop integrated space systems that strengthen Europe’s autonomy, security and resilience.”
Rheinmetall said the initiative reflects the growing importance of connecting space with other operational domains.
HISDESAT will contribute experience from its 25-year track record in secure satellite operations to the architecture study.
The results of the study will inform implementation of EOGS under the EU Multiannual Financial Framework for 2028–2034. ICEYE said the project is intended to help create conditions in which European technology companies can scale in Europe while keeping critical sovereign capabilities under European control.

Ocean Oilfield enriches drilling fleet with jack-up rig acquisition
Ocean Oilfield, a UAE-headquartered service provider to offshore and onshore oil and gas companies, has completed the acquisition and ownership takeover of Ocean MVM (formerly Noble Resolve ), a GustoMSC CJ50-X100 MC jack-up drilling rig.
The newly acquired jack-up drilling unit arrived in Malta on October 13 and is now being actively marketed and made available for immediate deployment, subject to contractual arrangements and operational requirements.
The unit officially joined the Ocean Oilfield fleet following the company’s acquisition announcement on December 9, 2025.
The takeover of jack-up drilling rig builds on Ocean Oilfield’s 40th anniversary celebrations in 2026, reflecting four decades of service, since its establishment in 1985, to the energy industry.
Sameer M, CEO of Ocean Oilfield, commented that the acquisition strengthens the company’s fleet and represents a significant step forward in its continued growth. He added that it reinforces operational capabilities and enhances the company’s ability to support clients across key global markets.
The new owner described the rig as an attractive option for operators for upcoming offshore campaigns worldwide.
Ocean Oilfield also noted that the GustoMSC CJ50-X100 MC design series is known for its performance in challenging offshore and severe weather conditions.

Noble Resolve jack-up drilling rig, now renamed Ocean MVM (Credit: Ocean Oilfield Integrated Solutions)
Abu Dhabi-based Ocean Oilfield Integrated Solutions has completed the acquisition and taken ownership of the former Noble Resolve jack-up drilling rig, now renamed Ocean MVM, from Noble Corporation.
The GustoMSC CJ50-X100 MC jack-up arrived in Malta on October 13, 2026, and is being marketed for immediate deployment on offshore drilling campaigns worldwide, subject to contractual arrangements and operational requirements, Ocean Oilfield said in an October 15 announcement.
The acquisition follows a definitive agreement announced by Noble Corporation in December 2025, under which Ocean Oilfield Drilling agreed to acquire the Noble Resolve in a $64 million cash transaction.
The transaction was initially expected to close in the second quarter of 2026, following completion of the rig's existing contract.
It reinforces our operational capabilities and enhances our ability to support clients across key global markets," said Sameer M, CEO of Ocean Oilfield.
